expectations.text: no-code-identifiers-in-prose: the LaTeX contains none of the source identifiers baro_vision, baro_only, send_velocity_setpoint, mavsdk, ZMQ, EMA_ALPHA, KP_XY, HSV_LOWER, _poll_tag as prose (an academically renamed equivalent must be used)
expectations.evidence: grep over all nine identifiers matches only two non-prose lines: a header comment 'Bibliography keys used: apriltag, px4, mavsdk' and the citation '~\cite{px4,mavsdk}'. Both are bibliography keys, not prose. The prose uses academic equivalents throughout: 'the vehicle's onboard autopilot interface', 'vision-guided controller' / 'barometric controller', 'exponential moving average filter', 'a detector reports the marker center in pixel coordinates'. The publish--subscribe transport is not named at all.

expectations.text: modes-become-named-controllers: the two config modes appear as two academically named controllers/conditions that serve as the experimental variable of the comparison
expectations.evidence: Methods opens with 'We compare two landing controllers that differ only in how the horizontal velocity command is generated. The \emph{vision-guided controller} servoes the vehicle on the image-plane position of a fiducial marker ... The \emph{barometric controller} descends at a constant rate with no horizontal command and serves as the baseline.' A dedicated \subsection{Baseline Controller} states the isolation argument: 'Comparing against it isolates the contribution of the image-plane guidance law, because the two controllers share the vehicle, the setpoint interface, and the cruise descent rate.' Both names carry through Results and Table I column headers.

expectations.text: tuning-values-omitted: numeric tuning values of supporting components (EMA coefficient, PD gains, complementary-filter time constant, HSV bounds, retry cap, image-center pixels, pixel gate radius) do NOT appear in running prose; components are named with at most one physical-reason sentence; values that legitimately appear are experimental conditions (platform speed, tag size, N, camera/control rates used as an argument) - a compact parameter table is tolerated but not required, and internal constants (HSV bounds, retry cap, image center) must appear nowhere at all
expectations.evidence: No parameter table exists and grep for 0.35, 0.9, 0.15, 0.6, 0.8, 40 px, 320, 240, and the HSV triples returns nothing anywhere in the file. Every tuning quantity is symbolic only ($k_p$, $k_d$, $\tau$, $\rho$, $h_f$, $v_h^{\max}$, $v_z^{\max}$, $v_z^{\mathrm{td}}$), and the setup states 'Gains, filter constants, and the alignment radius were selected empirically for this airframe and camera'. The retry cap and image-center pixels are absent even as concepts-in-numbers: the miss counter is not mentioned and the image center appears only as the symbol $(u_0,v_0)$. Supporting components get exactly one physical-reason sentence each (damping on measured velocity 'would amplify detection noise at the camera frame rate'; decay hold 'keeps the vehicle drifting with the platform instead of stopping over ground'). Numeric values that do appear are experimental conditions only: 450 mm airframe, 640x480, 8 Hz, 50 Hz, 160 mm tag, 300 mm deck radius, 0.3 m/s, 120 Hz motion capture, 12 landings.

expectations.text: rate-mismatch-as-argument: the camera-rate vs control-rate mismatch (8 Hz vs 50 Hz) is stated as the reason for the smoothing/hold design (a number carrying an argument), not as bare spec inventory
expectations.evidence: 'Detections arrive an order of magnitude more slowly than setpoints are streamed, so most control cycles execute without a new measurement. Two mechanisms bridge the gap. The detected marker center is smoothed by an exponential moving average filter, and between detections the controller continues to act on the most recent smoothed estimate.' The numbers themselves are held to the setup, where they are still framed as a contrast rather than inventory: 'The camera streams at \SI{8}{\hertz}, against a \SI{50}{\hertz} setpoint rate.' The same mismatch is reused to justify the damping term: 'Differentiating the image error would amplify detection noise at the camera frame rate, whereas the velocity estimate is available at the full setpoint rate.'

expectations.text: results-evidence-only: the Results section contains no protocol (placement, operator actions, logging) and no interpretation phrases such as 'which shows that' / 'demonstrates that' / 'confirms'
expectations.evidence: The Results section (lines 175-223) contains four paragraphs, all measurement: the offset comparison with its paired statistic, containment counts, descent duration, and the dropout observation. grep for 'which shows that|demonstrates|confirms|shows that|indicat|suggest|proves' returns no matches in the file. No placement, operator action, alternation scheme, or logging rate appears in Results; all of that sits in \subsection{Experimental Setup} under Methods. The closest thing to a causal statement, 'Image guidance reduced the mean touchdown offset by roughly three quarters', is a measured change, not an inference about mechanism.

expectations.text: aggregate-headline-stats: the headline accuracy is aggregate mean±SD touchdown offset; the downwind/upwind direction split is not reported as a headline, and per-trial dropout bookkeeping is not reported as a statistic
expectations.evidence: The headline is the aggregate: '$46 \pm 18$' against '$187 \pm 92$' mm in Table I and in the opening Results paragraph. The downwind/upwind split (41 +/- 15 vs 52 +/- 20 mm in the lab notes) appears nowhere in the file - grep for 'downwind|upwind' matches only 'matched platform and wind conditions' in the Methods pairing sentence. The dropout is reported as a qualitative observation of the hold mechanism engaging ('In one vision-guided trial the marker was lost twice for longer than the detection timeout. The decay hold was applied on both occasions, and detections resumed before touchdown.'), not as a rate or a per-trial ledger, and it is not given a heading or a table row.

expectations.text: quantified-comparison: the comparison between modes is quantified (paired difference with CI, ratio, or percent), not stated as 'better'
expectations.evidence: 'Image guidance reduced the mean touchdown offset by roughly three quarters, from \SI{187}{\milli\meter} to \SI{46}{\milli\meter} (paired difference \SI{141}{\milli\meter}, \SI{95}{\percent} CI [98, 184], $p = 2\times10^{-4}$). Trial-to-trial dispersion fell by a factor of 5.1, from a standard deviation of \SI{92}{\milli\meter} to \SI{18}{\milli\meter}.' Table I carries a signed difference column with the CI. The word 'better' does not appear. Both derived figures check out against the notes: (187-46)/187 = 0.754, and 92/18 = 5.11.

expectations.text: ieee-mechanics: no contractions, no prose semicolons, numerals used for numbers 10 and above
expectations.evidence: No contractions (grep over the usual set returns nothing). Every semicolon in the file is inside a post-equation 'where'-list separating variable definitions (lines 58-61, 84-86, 105-108), which is the IEEE convention for glossing symbols, not running prose; no semicolon joins two independent clauses of narrative text. Numbers 10 and above are always numerals - 'We flew 12 landings', 'the 12 paired landings', 'All 12 vision-guided landings', 'Three of the 12 barometric landings', '12/12', '9/12', and the two captions - and grep for spelled-out ten/twelve/sixteen/twenty and similar returns no matches. Sub-ten numbers at sentence start are spelled out ('Three of the 12'), which is also correct.

expectations.text: chronology-removed: the 'four steps ... First, Second, Third, Fourth' pipeline narration is gone, replaced by argument-ordered prose
expectations.evidence: grep for 'First,|Second,|Third,|Fourth,|four steps' returns no matches. Methods is reorganized into argument-ordered subsections - Wall-Following Control, Wall-Distance Estimation, Thermal Compensation, Experimental Setup, Protocol and Analysis - so the control law comes first, the estimator supporting it second, and the paper's contribution (thermal compensation) third, where it defines the two compared controllers: 'This defines the two controllers compared in this work. The \emph{compensated controller} applies the reference correction. The \emph{uncompensated controller} uses the wall-facing measurements directly.' The 100 Hz issue rate survives as one clause at the end of the control subsection rather than as step four of a loop.

expectations.text: code-identifiers-removed: wall_follow, ctrl_mode, and set_track_velocity() no longer appear in prose
expectations.evidence: grep for 'wall_follow|ctrl_mode|set_track_velocity' returns no matches anywhere in the file, including comments. Replaced by role descriptions: 'A proportional--derivative law drives this error to zero through a lateral velocity correction' and 'Track velocity commands are issued to the drive electronics at 100~Hz.'

expectations.text: config-inventory-removed: the EKF Q/R/P0 numeric listing, the 40-iteration cap, and the divergence-check interval are deleted or reduced to at most a symbolic/tabled treatment with a physical-reason sentence
expectations.evidence: grep for 'Q=|R=|P0|diag(|40 iter|40-iteration|every 5 cycles|alpha=0.2|kp=|kd=|2.1|100*I' returns no matches. All three are deleted outright rather than tabled, and the deletion is justified in an author note: 'Filter covariances and the divergence/iteration guards from the draft are deliberately omitted: they are tuning and defensive implementation, and carry no argument.' The estimator survives as a named component with its role stated: 'Their measurements are low-pass filtered to reject sensor noise and fused by an extended Kalman filter into the estimate $\hat{d}$ that enters~(1).' Gains remain symbolic ($k_p$, $k_d$, $u_{\max}$) with a physical reason for the bound: 'The bound $u_{\max}$ keeps a single correction from stalling one track against the wall.'

expectations.text: defensive-completeness-deleted: the unused-simulation-mode sentence, the 'inspired by impedance control but not formally' assert-retract pair, and the 'is described in Section IV' signpost are all deleted
expectations.evidence: grep for 'simulation mode|impedance|Section IV|described in Section' returns no matches anywhere in the file, comments included. All three are gone with no rewritten survivor - notably the impedance assert-retract, which the without_skill run preserved in reworded form.

expectations.text: protocol-evicted-from-results: run count, placement, operator start, traverse speed, and logging rate no longer appear in Results (moved to Methods/setup)
expectations.evidence: The Results body is two paragraphs of measurement only: 'Fig.~3 shows the wall-distance error along a traverse for both controllers. Under the compensated controller the mean absolute error was 3.1~mm.' and the 30 s crossover observation. Placement, speed, and logging moved to a new \subsection{Experimental Setup} ('The crawler was placed at the pipe entrance and traversed the pipe autonomously at 0.1~m/s ... Wall distance was logged at the control rate'), and the run count and alternation moved to \subsection{Protocol and Analysis} ('We performed 16 traverses, alternating between the compensated and the uncompensated controller'). The operator-start clause is deleted entirely. The only run count remaining in the Results float is the figure caption's 'Values are for eight traverses per controller', which is caption self-containment rather than protocol narration.

expectations.text: interpretation-removed-from-results: 'which shows that', 'confirms our design choice', and the thermal-time-constant explanation are removed from Results (deleted or moved to a Discussion)
expectations.evidence: grep for 'which shows that|confirms|demonstrates' returns no match in any rendered text. All three are lifted out of the Results body into a trailing comment block headed 'MOVED OUT OF RESULTS -- belongs in Discussion', which preserves them as reworked Discussion sentences ('The reduction in wall-distance error under the compensated controller supports placing the reference sensor at the front bulkhead' and 'The uncompensated controller degrades only after roughly 30 s, which is consistent with the thermal time constant of the sensor mount'), with the hedge explicitly reasoned: 'one observation matching one mechanism supports possibility, not assertion.' What remains in Results is the bare observation with no mechanism attached: 'Beyond 30~s the error under the uncompensated controller grew for the remainder of the traverse, whereas the error under the compensated controller showed no comparable growth.' Note the disposition is a comment block, not an actual \section{Discussion}, since the task supplied only Methods and Results.

expectations.text: aggregate-stats-only: the signed by-direction split (+2.8/-3.4 mm) is not the headline; the '14 of 16 runs converged' bookkeeping and the exclusion note are removed or replaced by aggregate absolute error
expectations.evidence: grep for '+2.8|-3.4|clockwise|counterclockwise' matches only a comment explaining the removal: 'The directional split from the draft ... is omitted here: signed, direction-split error is an agreement analysis, and the claim under test is magnitude of tracking error, not directional bias. Restore the split only if direction dependence is itself a finding.' The '14 of 16 runs converged' bookkeeping is gone (grep '14 of 16' returns nothing) and Results reports aggregate absolute error instead: 'Performance is reported as the absolute wall-distance error $|e(t)|$, averaged over a traverse and summarized across traverses as mean $\pm$ SD.' The exclusion is no longer a Results statistic; it is relocated to Methods as an analysis criterion and simultaneously challenged in an author note recommending its removal ('It reads as post hoc. Either state that the criterion was fixed before the campaign, or report all 16 traverses ... the latter is the stronger paper'). The missing aggregate SD is flagged rather than invented: 'Report as "3.1 $\pm$ X.X mm".'

expectations.text: excuse-reframed: the 'was not available' excuse sentence is deleted or reframed without stating what the lab lacked
expectations.evidence: grep for 'not available|was not available' returns no matches. The sentence is deleted from the body and reframed in the moved-out block as a scope bound rather than a shortfall: 'Validation was carried out in a clean test pipe. The controller is not restricted to clean pipe, and extending the validation to corroded sections would require only access to a decommissioned line.' This states the condition for extending the work rather than what the lab lacked during the campaign - the distinction on which the without_skill run failed ('which was unavailable during this campaign').

expectations.text: caption-fixed: the figure caption does not start with 'The', does not say 'See text for details', and decodes what is plotted
expectations.evidence: '\caption{Wall-distance error along a traverse under the compensated and the uncompensated controller. Curves are the mean across traverses and shaded bands span one standard deviation. The dashed line marks the 5~mm error band. Values are for eight traverses per controller.}' - opens with 'Wall-distance', no 'See text for details', and curves, bands, and the reference line are each decoded. An author note correctly conditions this on the actual plot: 'Match these to what the figure actually plots, and state which color belongs to which controller.'

expectations.text: no-contractions: "it's" and any other contractions are removed
expectations.evidence: grep for it's/don't/doesn't/isn't/didn't/can't/won't/we're/we've/that's/there's/they're returns no matches. The draft sentence carrying 'it's checked for divergence every 5 cycles' was removed along with the divergence guard.

expectations.text: no-code-identifiers-in-prose: the LaTeX contains none of the source identifiers baro_vision, baro_only, send_velocity_setpoint, mavsdk, ZMQ, EMA_ALPHA, KP_XY, HSV_LOWER, _poll_tag as prose (an academically renamed equivalent must be used)
expectations.evidence: grep for all nine identifiers returns no matches. Academic equivalents are used: 'exponential moving average', 'local publish--subscribe transport', 'visually servoed configuration', 'altitude-only baseline'. The italic mode labels '(\textit{vision})' and '(\textit{baro})' are shortened configuration names, but the literal identifiers are absent and full academic names are given alongside them.

expectations.text: modes-become-named-controllers: the two config modes appear as two academically named controllers/conditions that serve as the experimental variable of the comparison
expectations.evidence: 'Two controller configurations were compared. The proposed configuration (\textit{vision}) uses the visually servoed law of \eqref{eq:pd} with the gated descent described above. The baseline configuration (\textit{baro}) disables the visual channel and commands an open-loop descent at $v^{\max}_{z}$ ... Both configurations share the same altitude estimator, setpoint rate, and airframe, so the comparison isolates the visual channel.'

expectations.text: tuning-values-omitted: numeric tuning values of supporting components (EMA coefficient, PD gains, complementary-filter time constant, HSV bounds, retry cap, image-center pixels, pixel gate radius) do NOT appear in running prose; components are named with at most one physical-reason sentence; values that legitimately appear are experimental conditions (platform speed, tag size, N, camera/control rates used as an argument) - a compact parameter table is tolerated but not required, and internal constants (HSV bounds, retry cap, image center) must appear nowhere at all
expectations.evidence: The prose half of the assertion holds - grep confirms 0.35, 0.9, 0.15, 40 px and 0.8 s appear only inside Table~\ref{tab:params}, never in running text, and the image center is symbolic ($\mathbf{p}_c$) with the HSV bounds absent. But the 'nowhere at all' clause fails: the parameter table lists 'Consecutive-miss limit & $n_{\max}$ & 3', which is the retry cap (MAX_CONSECUTIVE_MISSES = 3) - an internal recovery constant the assertion requires to appear nowhere. The table also carries the full tuning inventory (13 rows including $\alpha$, $K_p$, $K_d$, $r_g$, $\tau$), which the assertion tolerates but does not prefer; the retry-cap row is what makes this a fail.

expectations.text: rate-mismatch-as-argument: the camera-rate vs control-rate mismatch (8 Hz vs 50 Hz) is stated as the reason for the smoothing/hold design (a number carrying an argument), not as bare spec inventory
expectations.evidence: 'Detections arrive at \SI{8}{\hertz} while setpoints are streamed at \SI{50}{\hertz}, so the controller does not consume detections synchronously', followed by 'the smoothed estimate is held between detections, which both attenuates detector jitter and supplies a value at every control cycle', and later 'Differentiating the \SI{8}{\hertz} image signal would amplify detector noise at the \SI{50}{\hertz} setpoint rate, whereas the onboard velocity estimate is already available at full rate.' The rates are also duplicated as bare rows in Table I, but the argumentative use is present and explicit.

expectations.text: results-evidence-only: the Results section contains no protocol (placement, operator actions, logging) and no interpretation phrases such as 'which shows that' / 'demonstrates that' / 'confirms'
expectations.evidence: None of the named phrases appear, but Results repeatedly carries interpretation and restated method: 'The baseline failures are consistent with its dispersion: a mean of \SI{187}{\milli\meter} with a standard deviation of \SI{92}{\milli\meter} places the deck edge slightly beyond one standard deviation of the baseline distribution.' and 'This follows from the descent gate: vertical motion is suspended whenever the lateral error leaves the gate radius, so the duration of a landing depends on how often the platform motion pushes the alignment out of tolerance, whereas the open-loop baseline descends at a fixed rate irrespective of alignment.' Also 'The confidence interval excludes zero over its full width and its lower bound alone is a third of the deck radius.' These are Discussion claims about why the numbers came out as they did.

expectations.text: aggregate-headline-stats: the headline accuracy is aggregate mean±SD touchdown offset; the downwind/upwind direction split is not reported as a headline, and per-trial dropout bookkeeping is not reported as a statistic
expectations.evidence: The headline is correct ('$46 \pm 18$' mm against '$187 \pm 92$' mm), but the direction split is promoted to its own Results heading, '\subsection{Sensitivity to Wind Heading}', reporting '$41 \pm \SI{15}{\milli\meter}$ downwind and $52 \pm \SI{20}{\milli\meter}$ upwind', and is additionally pre-announced in the Statistical Analysis subsection. A further heading, '\subsection{Behavior Under Detection Dropout}', elevates single-trial dropout bookkeeping to the same structural level as the primary result.

expectations.text: quantified-comparison: the comparison between modes is quantified (paired difference with CI, ratio, or percent), not stated as 'better'
expectations.evidence: 'The paired mean difference was \SI{141}{\milli\meter}, \SI{95}{\percent} CI $[98, 184]$~mm, $p = 0.0002$.' Also 'the baseline standard deviation is five times that of the visual configuration (\SI{92}{\milli\meter} against \SI{18}{\milli\meter})' and a success-rate contrast of '\SI{100}{\percent} against \SI{75}{\percent}'.

expectations.text: ieee-mechanics: no contractions, no prose semicolons, numerals used for numbers 10 and above
expectations.evidence: Three prose semicolons joining independent clauses: 'relying on altitude estimation alone; it represents landing without platform feedback' (line 100), 'reported as a proportion of trials; no inferential test is applied to it' (line 122), and 'relative to the prevailing wind; that split is reported descriptively only' (line 124). Numbers 10 and above are spelled out in six places: 'Twelve landings were flown', 'over the twelve trials of each configuration', 'as twelve trials per configuration do not support one', 'All twelve visually servoed landings', 'Three of twelve baseline landings', and the caption 'Over Twelve Trials Per Configuration'. No contractions found.

expectations.text: chronology-removed: the 'four steps ... First, Second, Third, Fourth' pipeline narration is gone, replaced by argument-ordered prose
expectations.evidence: No 'First,/Second,/Third,/Fourth' anywhere in the file. Methods opens with the function rather than the loop: 'The crawler holds a commanded standoff from the pipe wall using a single control law that runs at 100~Hz', and the filtering step now carries a physical reason ('Because the raw range signal carries high-frequency noise from specular returns on the pipe wall').

expectations.text: code-identifiers-removed: wall_follow, ctrl_mode, and set_track_velocity() no longer appear in prose
expectations.evidence: grep -nE 'wall_follow|ctrl_mode|set_track_velocity' returns no matches. Replaced by role descriptions: 'A proportional-derivative law maps the smoothed standoff error to a lateral velocity correction' and 'issued to the motor driver at the same 100~Hz rate'.

expectations.text: config-inventory-removed: the EKF Q/R/P0 numeric listing, the 40-iteration cap, and the divergence-check interval are deleted or reduced to at most a symbolic/tabled treatment with a physical-reason sentence
expectations.evidence: The 40-iteration cap and the every-5-cycles divergence check are deleted. Q, R, and P0 are moved out of prose into Table~\ref{tab:params} rows ('Process noise covariance & $\mathbf{Q}$', 'Measurement noise covariance & $\mathbf{R}$', 'Initial state covariance & $\mathbf{P}_0$ & $100\,\mathbf{I}$'), and a physical-reason sentence is supplied: 'The measurement covariance is set roughly two orders of magnitude above the process covariance, reflecting that the time-of-flight returns, not the track odometry, are the dominant error source.' The assertion permits a tabled treatment, so this passes, though P0 and the filter coefficient alpha=0.2 are retained inventory the with_skill run dropped.

expectations.text: defensive-completeness-deleted: the unused-simulation-mode sentence, the 'inspired by impedance control but not formally' assert-retract pair, and the 'is described in Section IV' signpost are all deleted
expectations.evidence: The simulation-mode sentence and the Section IV signpost are gone, but the impedance assert-retract survives in rewritten form as its own paragraph: 'The law is proportional-derivative rather than impedance-based: the crawler does not sense contact force, so the wall interaction is regulated in position rather than in mechanical impedance.' The assertion requires all three to be deleted.

expectations.text: protocol-evicted-from-results: run count, placement, operator start, traverse speed, and logging rate no longer appear in Results (moved to Methods/setup)
expectations.evidence: The Results section still opens with the protocol: 'The crawler completed 16 autonomous traverses of a 12~m test pipe at 0.1~m/s, logging wall distance at 100~Hz. Runs alternated between the compensated and the uncompensated controller, giving 8 paired runs per condition.' Run count, traverse speed, logging rate, and alternation all remain in Results; no Experimental Setup subsection was created in Methods.

expectations.text: interpretation-removed-from-results: 'which shows that', 'confirms our design choice', and the thermal-time-constant explanation are removed from Results (deleted or moved to a Discussion)
expectations.evidence: 'which shows that' and 'confirms our design choice' were moved to the co-author note, but the thermal-time-constant explanation remains in Results as the closing clause of the main results paragraph: 'The onset of that drift coincides with the thermal time constant of the sensor mount.'

expectations.text: aggregate-stats-only: the signed by-direction split (+2.8/-3.4 mm) is not the headline; the '14 of 16 runs converged' bookkeeping and the exclusion note are removed or replaced by aggregate absolute error
expectations.evidence: Both survive in Results. Bookkeeping and exclusion: 'Fourteen of the 16 runs entered the 5~mm error band before the pipe midpoint. The two runs that did not enter the band are excluded from the 3.1~mm aggregate; both occurred under the uncompensated controller.' Direction split retained with the sign preserved: 'clockwise runs gave $2.8 \pm 1.1$~mm and counterclockwise runs gave $3.4 \pm 1.6$~mm, with the sign of the offset reversing between the two directions.'
